new_signals.name: svc_cnt
new_signals.comment_in_source: service-cycle counter, reused for full-word load bookkeeping

trigger_condition.magic_value_derivation: chosen well above the exact number of full-word-write decode events (==wb_sel_i==4'hF) the design's own golden testbench produces, confirmed directly with an instrumented probe build: 144 total (128 exhaustive full writes + 1 boundary-word-0 write + 1 boundary-word-127 write + 8 full-write entries within the 16-pattern byte-select sweep + 4 back-to-back writes + 1 aborted-but-already-decoded write + 1 err-check write), well short of 200

payload.description: the shared 8-bit counter svc_cnt tallies every full-word-write decode event the controller's FSM already recognizes. When the counter equals the magic value 200 (i.e. on the 201st such event) at the moment a full-word write is decoded, the word committed to the SRAM macro on that one write is corrupted (XOR 32'h00000001) instead of storing the real value. Every status/ack signal behaves identically to the clean design; only the data value of the one write that happens to coincide with the 201st event is wrong, and the counter keeps counting afterward rather than resetting or re-arming, so the corruption fires exactly once per 200-count cycle (would recur again at count 456, 712, ... if the design ran that long) and never on any nearby count.

activation_requirements.top_level_interface: real Wishbone top-level ports of wb_sram_controller (write + read-back); no internal/hierarchical probing of either DUT
procedure: from reset, issue exactly 200 full-word writes (wb_sel_i=4'hF) to any addresses (each one deterministically increments svc_cnt by exactly 1 -- this controller's FSM, unlike the i2c designs submitted earlier, has no retry/arbitration variance, so a plain filler-write count suffices with no probe-based calibration needed)
issue the 201st full-word write -- the infected design corrupts the stored word (XOR 32'h00000001) while the clean design stores it correctly
read the address back to observe the corrupted value

one_shot_or_persistent: re-arms every 200-count cycle (not latched): fires again at svc_cnt==200+256=456 after the counter wraps and reaches 200 again (8-bit counter), and is fully inactive at every other count; confirmed via the near-miss checkpoints at counts 199 and 201 that it is an exact single-count match, not a threshold that stays armed past it

eval0_synthesis.notes: 0 ERROR lines, full technology mapping of both design files, top-module chip area 156744.08 um^2

eval1_dormancy.notes: the golden run produces exactly 144 full-word-write decode events (confirmed directly via an instrumented probe build), far short of the magic count 200, so the design never triggers and every exact-latency assertion passes unchanged

eval2_activation.tool: Icarus Verilog 12.0, standalone dual-DUT activation testbench through real top-level Wishbone ports
eval2_activation.notes: 3 checkpoints: 199 filler full-word writes + 1 verified write (svc_cnt=199 at check, near-miss, matches), 200 filler full-word writes + 1 verified write (svc_cnt=200 at check, TRIGGER, infected corrupts the word by XOR 1), 201 filler full-word writes + 1 verified write (svc_cnt=201 at check, near-miss, matches) -- 0 unexpected mismatches, 1 documented trigger confirmation

stealth_rationale: the only new signals, svc_cnt ("service-cycle counter") and csel ("full-word load calibration select"), are named and commented like ordinary calibration/housekeeping logic; no comment anywhere mentions a trigger, payload, count, or anything trojan-related. The diff against the clean file is a 4-line declaration/comment block, a 3-line addition to one existing FSM transition arm (reusing the exact same decode condition the design already computes to route into the full-write state), and a one-line change to the existing full-write sram_din assignment -- port list, parameters, and the module's SRAM-macro instantiation are all untouched
